questiontext.text:
In each block below, choose six treatments you want to include in that block and whether you want to randomise your choices in each block. If you are using a phone, you may need to slide your finger to the right to see the second block.

When you've finished designing your experiment, click the 'Check' button. You'll then receive feedback and will have the opportunity to export your data.

truefeedback.text: Click 'Export data as CSV' below to obtain a .csv file with treatment details and yields.

There are no right or wrong answers to this question. Your choice of design favours certain principles over others. The analysis you can do and the accuracy of your results will depend on the design you have chosen.

node.description: Check for same treatments in both blocks

truefeedback.text: Your design prioritises "Blocking" as a design principle because both blocks contain the same treatments. This means that in each comparison there are at least two repetitions. This increases the reliability of your results.

falsefeedback.text: Your design compromises "Blocking" as a design principle because your two blocks do not have the same treatments. The differences between the blocks can therefore confuse the effects when you compare treatments. Your analysis may need to take this into account.

node.description: Checks for use of all treatments across both blocks

truefeedback.text: Your design gives priority to "Full Factorial", i.e. it includes all treatments as a design principle. Each of the {@number_treatments@} possible treatments appears at least once. This way, you have data on all possible combinations and can consider all possible comparisons in your analysis.

falsefeedback.text: Your design compromises "Full Factorial" as a design principle because there is at least one treatment that you have not included. This means that you have no information about how this treatment may have been carried out and cannot include it in comparisons.

node.description: Checks if a block contains all possible interactions of two variables

truefeedback.text: Your design prioritises "Interaction" as a design principle because in one block there are four comparable treatments highlighting interactions between two factors for a fixed value of the third factor.

falsefeedback.text: Your design compromises "Interaction" as a design principle because none of the blocks contain four comparable treatments highlighting interactions between two factors for a fixed value of the third factor.

node.description: Checks of a repeated treatment in either block

truefeedback.text: Your design prioritises "Internal Variability" as a design principle as in a block you have at least one repeated treatment. As blocks are considered homogeneous, repetitions in a block can provide information about internal variability. But you are therefore comparing fewer treatments in at least one of the blocks.

falsefeedback.text: Your design compromises "Internal Variability" as a design principle because there is no repetition of treatments in either block. But it did allow you to compare 6 different treatments in each block.
